h1: Working part time at a brewpub while you study
title: Part-Time Brewpub Work While You Study | Craft Beer School
desc: How students can find part-time work at an Indian brewpub, the jobs on offer, what you will learn and how to turn it into a brewing career.
teaser: A part-time brewpub job will not make you a brewer overnight. It will show you whether you want to be one.
standfirst: Part-time work at a brewpub is one of the best ways for a student to test a brewing career. The jobs are usually front of house or cellar support, not brewing. Used well, they teach the trade from the ground up and open doors.
sections:
Most part-time roles at brewpubs are on the hospitality side: serving, bartending, hosting and events. Some brewpubs also take part-time help in the brewery for cleaning, kegging, moving stock and assisting on brew days. These are less common and usually go to people who have shown interest and reliability on the floor first.

Do not be put off by starting behind the bar. Serving beer every evening teaches you styles, guest preferences and how the draught system works. Many brewers began exactly there. Our guide on learning to brew while keeping a day job covers a similar balancing act for working adults.

Serving alcohol is age restricted in India and the minimum legal age to buy or serve varies by state. Some states also have rules on who may work in licensed premises. Check the rules where you live and make sure the brewpub follows them.

If you are an international student, check whether your visa permits part-time work at all. If you are a student under the legal drinking age in your state, look for roles in the kitchen or office instead and keep learning about brewing from books and courses until you are old enough.
What you learn on the floor

A brewpub floor is a fast education in beer. You will learn which styles guests order and why, how a wheat beer, a lager and an IPA differ in the glass and how temperature and pouring affect foam. You will see how the brewery's beers change over a keg's life.

You will also learn draught basics: kegs, gas, coolers and lines. Lines should be cleaned regularly. Draught quality guidance commonly recommends at least every two weeks. Ask to watch it done. Knowing why a beer suddenly tastes off from the tap is a skill many new brewers lack.

Once you have shown you are reliable, ask the head brewer if you can help on a brew day. Offer to come in early to clean. Brewery cleaning uses hot caustic, often around 1 to 2%, followed by acid. Both need proper training and protective gear, so do not handle them without either.

Most head brewers are short of time and appreciate someone who arrives on time, follows instructions and does not mind wet, heavy work. Ask questions at the right moments, not in the middle of a transfer. Within a few months you may be trusted with kegging, cellar checks or recording gravity readings.

Brewpub hours are evenings, weekends and festive peaks, which is often when exams and assignments fall too. Agree your hours with the manager in writing if you can and tell them early about exam periods. Many brewpubs are used to student staff and can be flexible if you are honest.

Look after yourself as well. Late shifts and early lectures are a hard mix. Do not drink on shift, even if colleagues offer a taste, unless it is a structured tasting the brewery runs for staff. Never drink and drive after a shift.
Make it count on your CV

Keep notes of everything you learn: styles poured, draught issues handled, brew days assisted, cleaning procedures followed. Ask the head brewer for a reference before you leave. A specific, positive reference from a brewer carries real weight when you apply for your first full-time brewery job.

If your studies are in science, engineering, hotel management or business, link them to the work. A microbiology student who has helped with yeast counts or a business student who has watched how a brewpub manages stock both have a strong story. Our guide on brewing equipment sales engineering shows one route for engineering students.

Pay for part-time hospitality work is modest. The value is in what you learn and who you meet. If after six months you find the brewery side tedious or the hours unbearable, you have learned something important cheaply. If you love it, you have a head start over classmates who only read about brewing.

Some students go on to work in distilleries or wineries instead. Our guide on working in an Indian distillery covers that path.

Make a short list of brewpubs within reach of your college. Visit two on a quiet weekday afternoon, ask for the manager and say you are a student interested in brewing who would like part-time work. Bring a one page CV that mentions any homebrewing, science subjects or hospitality experience. Follow up a week later.
faqs: Can students get part-time jobs at brewpubs in India?
Yes, mostly in serving, bartending and events. Brewery-side help with cleaning and kegging is less common and usually follows reliable floor work.
Is there a minimum age to work at a brewpub?
Serving alcohol is age restricted and the legal age varies by state. Check the rules where you live before applying.
Will working front of house help me become a brewer?
It helps. You learn styles, guest preferences and draught basics. You also build relationships with the brewing team.
No, apart from structured staff tastings the brewery runs. Never drink and drive after a shift.
